FreshWave Foods Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the FreshWave Foods Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss FreshWave Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Harper, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Rachel Ortiz, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, overall company performance highlights, organic revenue growth overall and by region, revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, and volume and price/mix analysis.

First, regarding progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: We've accelerated our 2030 Sustainability Roadmap, achieving key milestones in sourcing, water use, emissions reductions, and packaging that are enhancing margins and brand strength.

Second, concerning overall company performance highlights: We posted robust top-line growth across segments and regions, with margin expansion and strong cash flow generation underscoring our strategic momentum.

Third, in terms of organic revenue growth overall and by region: We saw balanced expansion led by North America and APAC, driven by volumes, pricing, and premium mix shifts.

Fourth, looking at revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Our results give us confidence to raise the outlook, reflecting favorable trends and operational leverage.

Fifth, reviewing e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: Digital channels continue to outperform, scaling to a larger share of our mix with superior margins.

Sixth, analyzing volume and price/mix analysis: Volumes rebounded steadily while price/mix delivered healthy gains through premiumization and disciplined actions.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Harper to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Harper (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Let me expand on those six key areas with more specifics, as they form the foundation of our performance.

Starting with progress on our sustainability initiatives and goals. As we wrap up our Q3 results, I want to update you on our advancements against our 2030 Sustainability Roadmap—a cornerstone of FreshWave Foods' strategy to deliver long-term value in the Food & Beverage sector. These initiatives go beyond compliance; they're generating tangible margin expansion, mitigating risks, and enabling premium pricing as consumers increasingly demand ESG-aligned products. Let me outline our four key pillars: sustainable sourcing, water stewardship, decarbonization, and circular packaging.

On sustainable sourcing, which makes up over 60% of our Scope 3 emissions, we've reached 92% responsibly sourced key ingredients globally, up from 78% last year and ahead of our 90% interim target. This covers 98% of our coffee from Rainforest Alliance-certified farms, consistent with progress at peers like Nestlé, along with 95% sustainable palm oil through our POIG membership to steer clear of deforestation risks. For cocoa, our expanded Cocoa Horizon program with Barry Callebaut now includes 85% of volume, aiding 45,000 smallholder farmers in West Africa with climate-resilient seedlings. In Latin America, sugar cane is at 97% via Bonsucro certification, while Asia is at 88% amid palm volatility—we're investing $50 million in FY24 for blockchain traceability pilots using IBM Food Trust to bridge that. These efforts have yielded 2-3% sourcing cost savings from 15% yield boosts in regenerative agriculture trials, directly improving our free cash flow conversion.

For water stewardship, vital for our water-stressed beverage lines like AquaPure and fruit juices, we've cut water intensity by 28% since the 2020 baseline, replenishing 115% of our footprint via 42 community watershed projects—surpassing benchmarks like PepsiCo's pep+ goal of 100% by 2030. In the U.S. Southwest, where 30% of bottling happens, membrane bioreactor retrofits slashed usage 35% at our Arizona plant. Europe improved 22% with rainwater harvesting amid EU Water Framework Directive pressures. Forward, $120 million in precision irrigation with IoT sensors across 150,000 hectares of supplier orchards targets another 10-15% drop by 2025, transforming water risks into advantages.

Regarding decarbonization, our SBTi-validated science-based targets are advancing well. Scope 1 and 2 emissions fell 42% year-over-year to 1.2 million tCO2e, powered by 55% renewable electricity in our 120 global plants—solar PPAs in India and wind in Brazil led the way. Scope 3, at 85% of total, saw 18% cuts via supplier programs, with 70% of Tier 1 suppliers SBTi-committed. Highlights include regenerative ag with General Mills on U.S. Midwest wheat cover cropping, sequestering 120,000 tCO2e yearly, and EV fleets in APAC targeting 40% electrification by 2026. We're 15% ahead of our 50% total GHG cut by 2030, aiding EU CSRD compliance and securing $500 million green bonds at 75bps below our curve.

Lastly, circular packaging: With 78% of Gen Z prioritizing recyclables per Nielsen, our eco-SKU lineup grew 12% YoY, like rPET AquaPure bottles. Recycled content averages 65%, up from 48%, with all PET bottles at 50%+ rPET. Virgin plastic dropped 32% since 2021, matching EU PPWR. North America's 75% aluminum can shift for carbonated drinks cut packaging GHG 25%, while enzymatic recycling pilots with Carbios processed 5,000 tons of PET in France. Landfill waste is 4%, food waste diversion up 22% via anaerobic digestion at 15 sites, yielding 20 GWh biogas.

These aren't just feel-good measures—they drove $180 million in cost avoidance last year, lifted our MSCI ESG to AA, and added 5 percentage points to brand preference per Kantar. We hedge risks like El Niño commodity swings with sustainable premiums. Ahead, $300 million FY25 capex targets net-zero factories, 100% sustainable packaging by 2030, and biodiversity net-positive through 1 million hectares restored. Full KPI dashboards in next month's ESG report.

Next, overall company performance highlights for Q3 2024. I'm thrilled with what we can call a standout quarter, highlighting the resilience and momentum of our portfolio in a challenging macro environment. Let's dive into the numbers.

Top line: net revenues of $3.2 billion, up 9% year-over-year reported and 11% in constant currency. Organic growth, excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and FX, was a strong 8%, our sixth straight quarter of expansion, beating the F&B industry average of 4-5% per NielsenIQ for packaged goods.

By segment, Beverages—including WaveCola carbonated soft drinks and HydroBoost functional waters—grew 12% organically to $1.4 billion. Premiumization shone: RTD coffees and plant-based OatWave grabbed 22% U.S. non-carbonated market share growth per IRI, with volumes up 5% on wellness hydration trends.

Snacks & Convenience Foods—FreshWave Crisps, protein bars, ready-to-eat meals—hit 7% organic growth to $1.1 billion. Mid-single-digit volumes despite soft demand, via 15% low-velocity SKU pruning for heroes like air-fried veggie chips up 35% YoY. Gross margins expanded 220 bps to 38.5% from wheat/oil hedges against Ukraine volatility.

International Foods—PureDairy yogurts, Asian sauces—delivered 6% organic to $700 million, emerging markets offsetting Europe.

Regionally, North America (65% revenues) grew 10% organically, U.S. retail up with e-commerce at 18% from 12%, via Amazon Fresh/Walmart+. Asia-Pacific 15% constant currency, China HydroBoost traction in Tier-1 cities vs. Mengniu, volumes +8%, new $50M Guangdong facility at 80% utilization. Europe flat organically on inflation/spending, but 7% pricing preserved margins.

Bottom line: adjusted operating income up 14% to $520 million, margins +110 bps to 16.3%. Gross margins +180 bps to 41.2% from $200M supply chain transformation—IBM Watson AI cut forecast error 25%, inventory 12%. Adjusted diluted EPS $0.78, +15% YoY, despite $0.03 FX hit.

Free cash flow $450 million, +20%, funding $300M repurchases and 7% dividend hike—our 28th straight. Net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, room for M&A like IndieSnack.

This validates HealthForward 2025: premium/sustainable at 45% portfolio (from 35%), digital with blockchain for 70% supply chain vs. EU regs, adjacencies like RTD protein shakes targeting $500M FY25. WaveClub app has 15M users, 2x repeats.

Now, organic revenue growth overall and by region. Organic came in at 5.4% for the quarter—beating our 3-4% guide, fifth straight acceleration quarter. First half FY2024 at 4.8%, on track for 4-5% full year. This shows portfolio strength amid inflation, supply normalization, premium health shifts.

Excludes PureHarvest APAC acquisition, 2% USD FX drag, EMEA canned divestiture. Drivers: +2.9% pricing across beverages/packaged foods; +1.8% volumes from RTD functionals/plant snacks; +0.7% mix from premium like VitaBoost Energy (15% beverage sales, up from 10%).

By region:

North America (55% revenue): 7.2%, up from Q1 6.1%. Volumes +3.4% > Nielsen, VitaFresh Protein Shakes +12% ACV to 85% at Walmart/Kroger. Pricing +3.5%, mix from premiums +20% YoY. Amazon Fresh partnership, trade optimization +15% ROI. Share gains vs. Monster/Chobani in $50B RTD.

EMEA (25%): 3.8%, per UK HFSS regs, soft sentiment. Volumes +0.2%, pricing +3.4% on wheat/dairy +20-25%, mix +0.2% from VitaOat up 28% Scandinavia. Pruned 12% impulse SKUs, Poland co-packing -25% lead times. 11% functional share per Kantar vs. Nestlé/Danone.

APAC (15%): 8.6%, accelerating. Volumes +4.1% on sparkling/BubbleVita +18% share Indonesia/Thailand vs. Topo Chico. Pricing +3.7%, mix +0.8% e-com 22% Shopee/Lazada. India distribution +30%.

Latin America (5%): 2.9% reported, underlying 4.5% sans -1.2% FX. Volumes +2.3% Brazil/Mexico hydration/snacks. Mitigated avian flu with Peru sourcing, precision fermentation pilots.

Validates Health-Premium-Core: 60% innovation functional, 22 new SKUs 85% velocity. Hedging 70% FY24, SAP accuracy ±5%.

Next, our revised full-year guidance. Building on Q3 organic 8.2% (5.1% volume, 3.1% price/mix), EBITDA margins +120 bps to 19.8% from Supply Chain 2.0.

We're revising up: organic net revenue 7-9% from 6-8%, total reported 8-10% CC, ~1% FX headwind.

Adjusted diluted EPS $5.25-$5.45 from $5.00-$5.20, 12-16% midpoint growth, with dividend/share buybacks ($500M repurchases, $1.5B authorization). Adjusted EBITDA $2.85-$2.95B, margins 22.5-23.0% (+150-200 bps).

By segment:

Beverages (52%): 9-11%, 6% volumes 'Hydrate Smart'/SparkVita (+2.5 share Nielsen), 3% price/mix, kombucha +25%. NA mid-teens, Tesco EMEA.

Snacking/Convenience (38%): 6-8%, volumes flat-+2% FuelBar, 4% premium mix. +11% vs. +3% savory IRI vs. Kellogg/Mondelez.

Health/Nutrition (10%): 12-14%, probiotics/shakes, e-com 18% from 12%.

Regions:

NA (65%): 8-10%, premium multipacks, dairy hedge limits COGS 1-2%.

Europe (20%): 6-8% CC, HFSS mitigated by low-sugar, regen ag slots at Carrefour.

APAC/LATAM (15%): high-teens, Indonesia/Brazil RTD teas +20%, Mercado Libre +$150M.

Assumptions: $200M input favorability (sugar -15%, corn -10%, freight), cocoa hedged 80% at $10k/MT, carob pilots. $350M productivity (Blue Yonder inventory -15%, Mexico auto +25%), margins 41.5-42.0%. Premium 'better-for-you' 40% sales +15% vs. core 4%, sustainability 60% factor. Macro: US CPI 2.5-3%, stable jobs.

This revision reflects execution to outperform peers.

Moving to e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue—one of our top engines. In F&B where traditional retail is ~75% per Nielsen, digital is key omnichannel. For us—premium plant snacks, TurboBoost energy drinks, meal kits—it's now 21% of net revenue, from 14% YoY.

Q3 e-com sales $252M, +45% YoY, +12% QoQ, outpacing 8% company to $3.2B total—wait, scaling note: adjusted for consistency. GMV $285M, DTC $98M (39%). AOV $48 +18% on 'Fuel & Go' bundles (32% attach).

Trend from FY21 8% amid 12% online grocery spike (IRI). FY23 +38%, FY24 25-30% projected. Margins +220 bps to 42.5%, lower slotting, fulfillment -15% via micro-centers.

US 68% ($171M +52%), Amazon/Instacart/Walmart+, TurboBoost +60% DoorDash. Europe 22% ($55M +32%) Ocado/Carrefour, subs 78%. APAC 10% ($26M +75%) Lazada/Shopee, Indonesia $5B market, drone pilots vs. spoilage.

$45M FreshFlow Shopify/AI (Dynamic Yield) lifted conversions 2.8-4.2%. Subs NutriBox 450k +60%, $120M recurring, LTV/CAC 4.2x. AR/VR build-a-box +22% basket. Snowflake CDP segments 18M users, Gen Z +35% AOV. Blockchain +28% eco buys.

Rebalances to DTC higher margins, JIT cuts waste 40%, elasticity 1.5x vs. inflation. To 25% revenue FY25, $400-450M +20-25%, $150M capex vs. fees/recession. Captures $1.5T e-grocery by 2027 (Statista).

Finally, volume and price/mix analysis. Organic 8% from 3% volume +5% price/mix—sixth quarter >7%, beating industry 4% (NielsenIQ).

Volumes +3% overall, rebound from Q2 1%. Beverages +5% cases (52M hectoliters +2.5M), Quench Zero +12% NA via Circle K 15k doors. Snacks +2%, Harvest Protein +18% EMEA vs. KIND/Clif in $12B protein (Euromonitor).

Regions: NA +4% (60%), OatFlex +25% oat 30% share. EMEA +3%, Zesty Crunch +8% UK/Germany. APAC +6%, RTD teas +10% China/India Tmall 20%. LATAM flat, micro-packs pruned SKUs 450-300.

Price/mix +5%: 3% pricing (4-6% core mature, flat EM), no elasticity drag (85% brand equity Kantar), private labels +2 IRI.

Mix +2%: premiums 35% from 28%, Quench Hydrate+ +22% ASP, plant dairy +15%, premium nuts +10%. Pruned 12% legacy. Palantir AI elasticity 50k SKUs, 2% hikes +50-75 bps margins. Recycled PET +0.5 mix.

For FY24 4-6% organic: $150M R&D low-sugar 20% portfolio 2025, omnichannel +8% away-home. Premium 40% revenues, hedging 70% cocoa/dairy Q1'25.

Net sales were $3.2 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.2%, impacted by productivity savings and favorable commodity dynamics. Operating income was $520 million, and earnings per share were $0.78. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for organic revenue growth to 7-9% and adjusted EPS to $3.10-$3.20.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Doe with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

John Doe (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflationary pressures on your business?

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, but we've navigated it effectively with pricing actions averaging around 7%, comprehensive hedging covering 70% of our key commodity needs like corn, sugar, and dairy, and productivity gains from our supply chain initiatives that offset escalations in wheat and oils. This preserved our margin expansion while maintaining volumes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Jane Smith (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for HydroBoost functional beverages and what is the expected impact?

David Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Jane. HydroBoost is a cornerstone of our premiumization, with plans to expand distribution via key partnerships like Amazon Fresh and new Tier-1 city launches in APAC. We're targeting 22% market share growth in non-carbonated functionals per IRI, driving 12-15% segment revenue uplift through wellness trends, higher AOV bundling, and e-com acceleration to capture hydration demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Lee with Barclays. Please proceed.

Bob Lee (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Rachel Ortiz (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Bob, thanks for the question. We've tackled disruptions head-on with our $200 million transformation, including AI demand sensing from IBM Watson reducing forecast errors 25% and inventory 12%, new facilities like Guangdong at 80% utilization, localization in Poland cutting lead times 25%, and blockchain for 70% traceability. These have boosted throughput 25%, mitigated avian flu and Red Sea issues, and positioned us for agility amid volatility.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Alice Chen with Citi. Please proceed.

Alice Chen (Citi):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Harper (CFO):
Alice, our outlook remains bright with the raised full-year guide reflecting Q3 momentum—7-9% organic growth, EPS $3.10-$3.20 midpoint up 10%, high-teens APAC/LATAM acceleration, and $200 million input tailwinds. We're focused on premium execution, productivity saving another $350 million, and monitoring CPI at 2.5-3%, confident in outperformance.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Reynolds for closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in FreshWave Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Adjusted op income +14% to $520M (margins +110bps to 16.3%), gross margins +180bps to 41.2%, EPS +15% to $0.78, FCF +20% to $450M.

Segment/region details provided, assuming input favorability and productivity.
